clue.text: Nothing in the ship that's exuberant in style

indicators.note: the word for nothing sits inside the word for the ship, so 'in' marks a container

parts.note: a barque is a sailing ship with three or more masts
nothing is zero, written as the round letter O

explanation.surface: A description of a vessel decorated in a florid, flamboyant style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside BARQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baroque was a period of ornate, extravagant art and architecture, so the word now describes any florid style.

clue.text: Horse-breaker about fifty is all swagger

indicators.note: the horse-breaker goes round the numeral, so 'about' marks a container

parts.note: a buster, or bronco-buster, breaks in wild horses
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A cowboy breaking horses, nearing fifty, is all bravado.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts BUSTER round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluster is loud, boastful talk, the same empty bravado as swagger.

clue.text: Merchants popular with Bo-Peep ?

parts.note: the nursery-rhyme shepherdess's sheep lost and regained their tails, so she would love anyone who supplied tails again

explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Little Bo-Peep's sheep come home 'bringing their tails behind them'; shopkeepers split as re-tailers would put tails back on.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailers are shopkeepers who sell goods to the public, a kind of merchant.

clue.text: "To the mighty of the earth, th'oppressor " (Milton)

definitions.text: "To the mighty of the earth, th'oppressor " (Milton)

parts.words: "To the mighty of the earth, th'oppressor " (Milton)
parts.note: the gap completes Milton's line in Samson Agonistes, a verb meaning to crush or subdue

explanation.walkthrough: Milton's Samson Agonistes has 'To quell the mighty of the earth, th'oppressor'; the solver fills the gap from the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means to subdue or put down, what the line says of the oppressor's fate.

clue.text: How to " adorn a tale "?

parts.note: to adorn a story is to add invented details, the same verb as decorating cloth with needlework

explanation.walkthrough: The verb means both to decorate fabric with needlework and to exaggerate a story with made-up detail.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish a story with invented details is to ornament it, the figurative sense of decorative stitching.

clue.text: Extremely open " handicaps " ?

parts.note: read 'handicaps' as hand-caps: coverings for the hands that leave the extremities, the fingers, unseparated and free of individual stalls

explanation.walkthrough: 'Handicaps' is split into hand + caps, a cap for the hand; 'Extremely open' points to a glove left open at the extremities rather than closed round each finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Mittens are hand coverings without separate fingers, which hamper what the hand can do, a literal handicap.

clue.text: Disguises request in writing

indicators.note: the request sits inside the abbreviation for writing, so 'in' marks a container

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A plea for disguises is put down on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ASK inside MS.
explanation.definitionFit: Masks are face coverings worn to conceal identity, so they are disguises.

clue.text: Top workers are men of straw

definitions.meaning: roofers work on the top of a house, putting on its covering
workers who roof houses with straw or reed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Men of straw' usually means people of no substance; here it is literal, roofers who work in straw.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmen who roof cottages with straw or reed work on top of the house, their material being straw.

clue.text: Come in, just for the record

definitions.meaning: to go into a room is to come in
to write an item into a ledger or register is to put it on record

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to go into a place and to write something into a register or ledger.

clue.text: He is in haste perhaps to put up his sword

indicators.note: the pronoun sits inside the jumbled letters, so 'in' marks a container
perhaps says the word haste is only one possible order of its letters, so they are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man hurriedly puts away his sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns HASTE into SATHE and 'in' puts HE inside it, after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a sword is to put it back in its scabbard, which is what putting up a sword means.

clue.text: Remove the O.B.'s badge ?

parts.note: an O.B., old boy, wears the old school tie as his badge; to remove a tie is to undo its knot

explanation.walkthrough: O.B. is old boy, a former pupil of a British school, whose emblem is the old school tie; taking that tie off is to un-tie it.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or a necktie is to loosen and remove it, the action the clue describes.

clue.text: Castellan of Cornwall ?

parts.note: a castellan is the governor of a castle, its boss; that phrase is also the name of a Cornish coastal village

explanation.walkthrough: Boscastle is a small harbour village on the north coast of Cornwall, in south-west England; split as 'boss castle' it describes the man in charge of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A castellan is the keeper or commander of a castle, its boss, and the Cornish village name splits into those words.

clue.text: There's something electric in roulades in plenty

indicators.note: the charged particle sits inside the word for the vocal runs, so 'in' marks a container

parts.note: roulades are runs of quick notes in singing, ornaments like trills
an ion is an electrically charged atom or particle

explanation.surface: A singer's florid runs crackle with electricity, and there are lots of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ION inside TRILLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Trillions are vast numbers, so to have something by the trillion is to have it in abundance.

clue.text: Is not in, mark that

definitions.meaning: the Latin word ... means 'it is lacking', literally what is missing from a text
a proofreader's inverted-V sign showing where something should be inserted

explanation.walkthrough: The proofreading sign takes its name from the Latin for 'it is missing', because it marks where omitted text belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin verb meaning 'is lacking' names the editor's symbol placed where a missing word must be inserted.

clue.text: With which the corybantic Scot winds up ?

definitions.text: With which the corybantic Scot winds up ?

parts.words: With which the corybantic Scot winds up ?
parts.note: a wildly dancing Scot ends the evening with lively dances, and a fishing Scot winds up his line on spools

explanation.walkthrough: Corybantic means wild and frenzied in dance; Scottish reels are fast country dances, and reels are also the spools on which line or thread is wound up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively Scottish country dances and the spools on which thread or fishing line is wound share this one word.

clue.text: Just the bird to flirt with William

parts.note: to spoon is an old word for to court or flirt amorously
Bill is a short form of the name William

explanation.surface: The perfect bird for a dalliance with a man called William.
explanation.walkthrough: To spoon, in old slang, is to kiss and cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The spoonbill is a wading bird with a long flat bill widening at the tip.

clue.text: On — seas long wont to roam" (Poe)

definitions.text: On — seas long wont to roam" (Poe)

parts.words: On — seas long wont to roam" (Poe)
parts.note: the missing word completes a line of Poe's poem 'To Helen', describing the wanderer's hopeless voyaging

explanation.walkthrough: Poe's 'To Helen' has 'On desperate seas long wont to roam'; the solver fills the gap from the poem.
explanation.definitionFit: In Poe's line the seas are reckless and hopeless, the adjective the quotation leaves out.

clue.text: Modestine was his fellow-traveller

parts.note: Modestine was the donkey in a Scottish author's account of walking through the Cévennes

explanation.walkthrough: Robert Louis Stevenson's 'Travels with a Donkey in the Cévennes' (1879) recounts his journey with a donkey called Modestine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish author of Treasure Island wrote of his walking tour with the donkey Modestine.

clue.text: "'Kings are by God ", the flockmaster taught

definitions.text: "'Kings are by God ", the flockmaster taught

parts.words: "'Kings are by God ", the flockmaster taught
parts.note: the gap holds the word of the divine right of kings, and a flockmaster, a shepherd, taught his sheep by pointing them

explanation.walkthrough: The divine right of kings says they are chosen by God; the word also suggests a shepherd guiding his flock by pointing, so the pastor taught the doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Appointed means chosen and installed in office, as the doctrine of divine right held kings were by God.

clue.text: There's talk of Pluto taking instruction

indicators.note: Pluto takes on the word for instruction, which follows straight after it in the answer

parts.note: Dis is another name for Pluto, Roman god of the underworld
a course is a programme of instruction or lessons

explanation.surface: Gossip that the god of the underworld has signed up for lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the Roman name for the underworld god Pluto; 'taking' joins it to COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a spoken or written discussion, a synonym of talk as a noun.

clue.text: Do I cast about for gangsters?

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are turned about and moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether to throw something around while looking for criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you to rearrange DO I CAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Dacoits are members of armed robber gangs in India and Burma, so they are bandits.

clue.text: Simpleton with a penny gets something tasty

parts.note: a sap is a foolish, gullible person
a means one, written as the Roman numeral I
d is the abbreviation for a penny in old British money

explanation.surface: A fool with a coin buys himself a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: D stood for penny in Britain's pre-decimal coinage, from the Latin denarius.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid means having a pleasant flavour, the quality of food that is savoury and good to eat.

clue.text: Betsey Trotwood's bêtes noires?

parts.note: David Copperfield's aunt waged war on the animals that strayed onto her lawn, the pet hates of the clue

explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's David Copperfield, Aunt Betsey Trotwood rushes out crying 'Janet! Donkeys!' whenever donkeys cross her green; bêtes noires are pet hates.
explanation.definitionFit: The animals Aunt Betsey chased off her lawn were the beasts of burden she most detested.

clue.text: Is there a taxi on the rank, boy ?

definitions.text: Is there a taxi on the rank, boy ?

parts.words: Is there a taxi on the rank, boy ?
parts.note: a waiting taxi on the rank is a ..., and with 'boy' after it the phrase names a ship's young servant

explanation.walkthrough: A taxi parked at the rank is a 'cab in'; add 'boy' and you have a cabin boy, a ship's young attendant, while the word alone is a small room aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room on a ship, whose young servant is the cabin boy, sounds like a taxi being in on the rank.

clue.text: How right to keep healthy!

parts.note: split in two, the word says to stay in good health, and as one word it means to suit or be right for

explanation.walkthrough: Split, the word reads 'be fit', keep healthy; whole, it means to be proper or right for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To befit is to be suitable or proper for, and split it advises staying in good health.

clue.text: No viper is endowed with such foresight

indicators.note: the letters of 'No viper is' are endowed with a new arrangement, recast as the word for foresight

explanation.surface: A remark that no snake has the gift of seeing what is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endowed with such' tells you to rearrange NO VIPER IS into a word of nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Prevision is knowledge of events before they happen, which is what foresight means.

clue.text: Numbers of trainees ?

parts.note: boys training for knighthood served as attendants, and the same word is the numbered leaves of a book

explanation.walkthrough: In medieval times a page was a boy in training to become a knight; the leaves of a book are numbered pages too.
explanation.definitionFit: Young attendants training for knighthood share their name with the numbered sides of a book's leaves.

clue.text: Where The Towers provided a saucy show ?

definitions.text: Where The Towers provided a saucy show ?

parts.words: Where The Towers provided a saucy show ?
parts.note: Marlowe's Faustus speaks of the topless towers of Troy, and topless suggests a racy cabaret

explanation.walkthrough: Marlowe wrote of Helen's face that it 'burnt the topless towers of Ilium', Ilium being Troy; topless suggests an undressed show.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilium is the Latin name of Troy, whose topless towers Marlowe made famous.

clue.text: Violates, in a laciniated way ?

parts.note: laciniated means fringed or jaggedly edged, so in a laciniated way is with fringes

explanation.surface: Asking whether something breaks the rules in a ragged, frayed manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Laciniated, a botanical term, means fringed; 'in a laciniated way' is 'in fringes', which runs together as one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe a rule or right is to break or transgress it, so the verb matches violates.

clue.text: The fibre of thistledown ? Hardly !

indicators.note: the fibre is taken out of the word thistledown, its letters running inside it

explanation.surface: Asking whether thistle fluff counts as a textile fibre, and answering no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' points into 'thistledown'; 'Hardly!' says the real fibre, from Mexican agave, is not thistledown at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a strong plant fibre from Mexican agave and yucca used for cordage and brushes.

clue.text: Makes final payments for seats

definitions.meaning: to settle a bill or debt is to pay it off in full
a settle is a wooden bench with a high back and arms

explanation.definitionFit: Paying off accounts in full is to clear them, and high-backed wooden benches are another sense of the word.

clue.text: A demon's in these rovers

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are found again, rearranged, in these wanderers' name

explanation.surface: A devil lurks among a band of wanderers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in these' says the letters of A DEMONS are all in the answer, shuffled; the possessive 's counts as an S here.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomades is an old form of nomads, people who wander from place to place without a fixed home.
